title: In This Valley You Fall APART If Your Family Forgets You
premise: In this valley, every body is built in blocks with thin seams between them, and if your family forgets you, your body comes apart, block by block. My blocks hang a finger's width apart because Dad, all the family I have, is forgetting me. For his sixtieth birthday he wants a balloon flight at dawn, just him and me, and the pilot Rosa takes us up over the mist. With each burner roar I come further apart, until Dad looks at me and asks Rosa who I am.
twist: Dad turned sixty four years ago. It is the last morning he remembers whole, with me in it, so Rosa flies us every dawn and I give him that birthday again: when I say what I said that morning he lands back in it and my blocks click shut. The wall of badges in her trailer is every one of those mornings, and by lunch he will ask who I am.
world: a hot-air balloon basket at dawn over misty farmland, a cold launch field and a farm kitchen, a field gate, a lane by a dry-stone wall and the inside of a pilot's trailer
